cluster_summary: These vulnerabilities arise from insufficient validation of external inputs (HTTP headers) and lack of uniform responses in password reset and email verification flows, leading to user enumeration, token leakage, and resource abuse.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled URLs or server-controlled redirect responses into HTTP clients that automatically follow redirects or reuse a previously validated URL decision. Report code paths where the final redirected scheme, host, port, and resolved address are not revalidated before the sensitive network request. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should disable automatic redirects or revalidate every redirect hop against the same allowlist and address policy.

mechanism.missing_guard: the final redirected scheme, host, port, and resolved address are not revalidated before the sensitive network request
mechanism.name: SSRF through redirect-following client
mechanism.sink_shape: HTTP clients that automatically follow redirects or reuse a previously validated URL decision
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled URLs or server-controlled redirect responses
mechanism.typical_fix: disable automatic redirects or revalidate every redirect hop against the same allowlist and address policy

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Make the response uniform regardless of user existence: always return the same HTTP status code, message, and redirect target.
sub_patterns.name: User enumeration via distinguishable HTTP responses
sub_patterns.root_cause: The password reset or email verification endpoint returns different HTTP status codes, response messages, or redirect targets based on whether the user exists or has an email configured, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to enumerate valid user identifiers.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Introduce a configured base URL or trusted hosts list, and validate the header against it before using it in link generation; reject requests where the header does not match.
sub_patterns.name: Unvalidated HTTP header in email link generation
sub_patterns.root_cause: The application constructs URLs for password reset or email verification emails using the HTTP Host or Origin header from the incoming request without validating that the header matches a trusted domain, allowing an attacker to inject a malicious domain and cause token leakage or open redirect.
